descriptions.alosHashachar: First light, with the sun 16.1° below the horizon — the degree equivalent of a 72-minute dawn, so it tracks the same twilight at any latitude or season.
descriptions.alos72: A fixed 72 minutes before sunrise (the time to walk 4 mil at 18 min each; Rambam and Rishonim) — the dawn the Magen Avraham uses for his proportional-hour zmanim.
descriptions.misheyakir115: Earliest tallit and tefillin — sun 11.5° below the horizon (≈52 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; the actual offset varies by place and season).
descriptions.misheyakir11: Sun 11° below the horizon (≈48 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; the actual offset varies by place and season).
descriptions.misheyakir102: Sun 10.2° below the horizon (≈45 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; the actual offset varies by place and season).
descriptions.sunrise: Sunrise (Hanetz). The vatikin complete the morning Shema just before this moment and begin the Amidah exactly at sunrise.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaMGA: End of the 3rd proportional hour by the Magen Avraham — the day measured from dawn (72 min before sunrise) to nightfall (72 min after sunset), an earlier deadline.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaGRA: End of the 3rd proportional hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA) — the day measured from sunrise to sunset.
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaMGA: End of the 4th proportional hour by the Magen Avraham — day measured from dawn (72 min) to nightfall (72 min).
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaGRA: End of the 4th proportional hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA) — day measured from sunrise to sunset.
descriptions.sofZmanAchilasChametzMGA: Latest time to eat chametz — end of the 4th proportional hour by the Magen Avraham (day measured from dawn, 72 min before sunrise, to nightfall, 72 min after sunset).
descriptions.sofZmanAchilasChametzGRA: Latest time to eat chametz — end of the 4th proportional hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA; day measured from sunrise to sunset).
descriptions.sofZmanBiurChametzMGA: Latest time to burn the chametz — end of the 5th proportional hour by the Magen Avraham (day measured from dawn, 72 min, to nightfall, 72 min).
descriptions.sofZmanBiurChametzGRA: Latest time to burn the chametz — end of the 5th proportional hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA; day measured from sunrise to sunset).
descriptions.chatzos: Solar noon — the midpoint of the day, halfway between sunrise and sunset.
descriptions.minchaGedola: Earliest time to pray Mincha — 6½ proportional hours into the day (a half-hour after midday).
descriptions.minchaKetana: Preferred time to pray Mincha — 9½ proportional hours into the day.
descriptions.plagHamincha: 10¾ proportional hours into the day (1¼ hours before sunset) — the earliest one may pray Maariv or accept Shabbat.
descriptions.candleLighting: Candle lighting before Shabbat / Yom Tov — the set minutes before sunset (18 by default; 40 is the Jerusalem custom).
descriptions.sunset: Sunset (Shkia) — Shabbat / Yom Tov begins, and the doubtful twilight (bein hashmashot) starts.
descriptions.tzaisGeonim: An early, lenient nightfall — sun 5.95° below the horizon (the Geonim / Baal HaTanya, ≈24 min after sunset in Jerusalem near the equinox). Some rely on it to end rabbinic fasts.
descriptions.tzais: Three small stars are visible — sun 8.5° below the horizon (≈36 min after sunset in Jerusalem near the equinox). A slightly stringent nightfall; the new day begins.
descriptions.tzais72: Rabbeinu Tam's stringent nightfall — a fixed 72 minutes after sunset (4 mil × 18 min). Relied on for ending Shabbat, Yom Tov, and Yom Kippur.
descriptions.chatzosLaila: Solar midnight — the halachic midpoint of the night, halfway between sunset and sunrise.
descriptions.tzais42: A fixed 42 minutes after sunset — a common practical nightfall some communities use to end Shabbat and Yom Tov.
descriptions.shaahZmanisMGA: The length of one proportional hour by the Magen Avraham — the day measured from dawn (72 min before sunrise) to nightfall (72 min after sunset), so the hour is longer.
descriptions.shaahZmanisGRA: The length of one proportional hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA) — the day measured from sunrise to sunset.

baseDescriptions.alos: Dawn — first light; the start of the halachic day for many mitzvot.
baseDescriptions.misheyakir: Earliest time to don tallit and tefillin — when there is enough light to recognize an acquaintance.
baseDescriptions.sofZmanShma: Latest time to recite the morning Shema — the end of the third proportional hour.
baseDescriptions.sofZmanTfila: Latest time for the morning Amidah (Shacharit) — the end of the fourth proportional hour.
baseDescriptions.achilasChametz: Erev Pesach: the latest time to eat chametz — the end of the fourth proportional hour.
baseDescriptions.biurChametz: Erev Pesach: the latest time to burn / dispose of the chametz — the end of the fifth proportional hour.
baseDescriptions.tzais: Nightfall — three stars are visible and the new halachic day begins.
baseDescriptions.shaahZmanis: The length of one halachic (proportional) hour — a twelfth of the halachic day; zmanim like sof zman Shema are counted in these hours. Shown as a duration (h:mm:ss), not a clock time.

panel.zmanimSettingsHint: More zmanim and opinions can be shown via the calendar settings.
panel.lehumraNote: Times are rounded to the stringent whole minute (lehumra).
panel.lehumraDetail:
Every displayed time is rounded to a whole minute in the stricter direction — by less than a minute, and only in the display; the underlying calculation stays exact.
Rounded DOWN (deadlines — no later than): sof zman Shema and Tefila, the chametz deadlines, shkia, candle lighting before Shabbat and Yom Tov, and the start of a fast.
Rounded UP (onsets — no earlier than): alot ha-shachar, misheyakir, hanetz, chatzot, mincha gedola and ketana, plag ha-mincha, tzeit ha-kochavim, havdala, the end of a fast, and candle lighting after nightfall (2nd Yom Tov night, Motzei Shabbat).
panel.observedPostponed: Observed later this year because of Shabbat.
panel.observedAdvanced: Observed earlier this year because of Shabbat.

learning.title: Daily learning
learning.dafYomiInfo: One page (daf) of the Babylonian Talmud a day; the worldwide cycle completes the entire Talmud in about 7½ years.
learning.yerushalmiYomiInfo: One page of the Jerusalem Talmud a day (Vilna edition); the cycle takes about 4¼ years. No page is learned on Yom Kippur or Tisha BeAv.
learning.mishnaYomitInfo: Two mishnayot a day, completing the entire Mishnah in about six years.
learning.nachYomiInfo: One chapter of Nevi'im (Prophets) or Ketuvim (Writings) a day, completing Nach in 742 days.
learning.tehillimInfo: Tehillim (Psalms) divided across the days of the Hebrew month — the whole book is finished every month.
learning.rambamInfo: One chapter of the Rambam's Mishneh Torah a day; the cycle completes all 14 books in just under three years.
learning.pirkeiAvotInfo: A chapter of Pirkei Avot is studied on Shabbat afternoons between Pesach and Rosh Hashanah.

settings.candleOffsetHint: Minutes before sunset (40 is common in Jerusalem).
settings.elevationHint: Adjusts sunrise, sunset and the zmanim measured from them for the location's height above sea level. Standard published times use sea level — enable this only if your community follows visible-horizon times. Degree-based zmanim, chatzot and candle lighting are unaffected. For the best result, use your device location rather than a city search — the elevation is then detected for your exact spot, not the city center.
settings.havdalaHint: Opinion for when Shabbat and Yom Tov end.
settings.learningDisplayHint: Choose which learning cycles appear in the day panel.
settings.zmanimDisplayHint: Choose which zmanim and opinions appear in the day panel.
